text:
maria_engineer: heads up - I got an email about a midyear plan amendment changing the employer match formula starting 2026-07-01 (50% up to 6% -> 100% up to 3%). Does this apply retroactively to contributions earlier in the year? Confused if my paychecks from Jan-Jun get recalculated.

leo_benefits: hey @maria_engineer :wave: short answer: typically plan amendments are effective on the stated effective date and not retroactive to previously-processed payroll. So match paid Jan-Jun stays as originally calculated. However, plan admin can adopt an "enhancement" that includes a true-up for the plan year if they choose. We'll confirm.

leo_benefits: important nuance: if the amendment is labeled an "improvement" and the board approves a true-up, payroll would need to submit an off-cycle file and the trustee would process additional employer contributions to bring eligible participants up to the new formula for the plan year. That requires funding approval and compliance check.

sarah_comp: chiming in from comp: if leadership wants a true-up, we need cost approval and sign-off from finance + execs. Also confirm whether the true-up counts toward annual contribution limits and how it shows on pay statements. Policy-wise, we usually avoid retroactive match changes unless there's a compelling retention/competitive reason.

maria_engineer: thanks. If they do a true-up, does vesting apply to the additional matched dollars based on original hire date or the true-up payment date?

leo_benefits: vesting follows the date the employer contribution is made. So a true-up paid later vests per the vesting schedule from the date of that contribution. That can be relevant for folks near a vesting cliff.

forus-rep: Forus here 44b - operational note: we can accept a "true-up" remittance file. Required fields: participant ID, contribution type (employer true-up), dollar amount, effective plan year. We need remittance at least 5 business days before end-of-month processing to include in that month's posting. Also, if payroll sends a lump sum true-up, include a mapping to original payroll periods for recordkeeping.

hr-director: FYI leadership asked comp to model cost impact. If we do a one-time retroactive true-up, we'll need to list impacted employees and projected cashflow. Also legal wants confirmation that the amendment doesn't violate plan non-discrimination rules.

maria_engineer: last Q - I'm 60+ and making catch-up contributions. Does a true-up interact with catch-up limits or create any tax differences?

leo_benefits: catch-ups (age 50+) are employee deferral catch-ups and don't change employer match rules. Employer true-up wouldn't be treated as catch-up; it's an employer contribution, subject to overall annual addition limits (415(c)) but not the age 50 deferral catch-up limit. For tax specifics, consult a tax advisor.

benefits-bot: Docs: https://benefits.redwood.example/plan-amendments (see "True-ups & Effective Dates")

leo_benefits: next steps: 1) benefits will confirm whether the amendment includes a true-up (today); 2) if yes, forus and payroll will coordinate file format and timing; 3) comp/hr will run cost/vesting impacts and we4e8ll announce details. I'll update this thread once I hear back.

maria_engineer: appreciate it, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
